learning_objective: 🎯 Learn how to read, write, append, and manipulate persistent data across Text Files, CSV Files, and Binary Files using Python.

key_vocabulary.definition: A sequence of bytes or characters flowing into (input) or out of (output) a Python program.
The process of serializing (converting) a Python object hierarchy into a byte stream for binary file storage.
The inverse process of converting a stored byte stream back into the original Python object.
A character (like a comma, tab, or pipe) used to separate individual data fields in a structured text file like CSV.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Text files store data as human-readable ASCII/Unicode characters where each line ends with an EOL (End-Of-Line, `\n`) character. Opened using modes: 'r' (read), 'w' (write - overwrites), 'a' (append - adds to end), and 'r+' (read and write).

Binary files store data in exactly the same format as it is held in memory (0s and 1s), making access faster and unreadable to text editors. Using `import pickle`, we use `pickle.dump(object, file_handle)` to write (serialize) and `pickle.load(file_handle)` to read (deserialize).

Comma-Separated Values (CSV) files store tabular data in plain text. Using `import csv`, we use `csv.reader(file_handle)` to read rows as lists, and `csv.writer(file_handle)` with `.writerow()` or `.writerows()` to export data.

Python tracks where it is reading/writing using a file pointer. `file.tell()` returns the current byte position of the pointer. `file.seek(offset, whence)` moves the pointer to a specific byte location (whence: 0=beginning, 1=current, 2=end).

exam_tips: 📌 When writing CSV files in Windows, always specify `newline=''` in `open()` to prevent an unwanted blank line from appearing between rows.
📌 In Binary file programs, `pickle.load()` throws an `EOFError` when it reaches the end of the file — always wrap binary reading loops inside a `try-except EOFError` block.
📌 Know the difference between `.read()` (reads entire file as a single string), `.readline()` (reads one line at a time), and `.readlines()` (reads all lines into a list of strings).
quick_recap: ⭐ Using the `with open(...) as f:` syntax is best practice because it automatically closes the file even if an exception occurs.
⭐ Opening a file in `'w'` or `'wb'` mode immediately truncates (erases) the existing contents of the file if it already exists.
⭐ Text files automatically perform line-ending translation across operating systems, whereas binary files read and write raw bytes untouched.
